editorial:
If you grew up reading the books or watching the earlier movies, you already know Greg Heffley is a kid who will do almost anything to avoid effort. This time, summer break is here, and all Greg wants is to sit inside, play video games, and hang out with his friends. His dad, though, has decided this is the perfect season for father-son bonding, which sounds like a nightmare to Greg. To escape that fate, he lies about having a job at a fancy country club, and that little fib quickly spirals into one awkward situation after another. The movie keeps things light and silly, with plenty of slapstick moments, family arguments, and the kind of embarrassing mistakes that feel very true to middle school life.

The pacing moves quickly, so younger viewers will stay engaged, and the humor lands best if you enjoy goofy, kid-friendly comedy rather than sharp wit. The cast does a solid job, especially the dad, who brings real warmth underneath the frustration. On the downside, some jokes feel stretched out, and the story can be predictable if you have seen the earlier films. Still, it is a fun, easy watch for families. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Greg's lies about the country club job finally catch up with him, and his dad discovers the truth. Instead of staying angry, his dad takes him on a camping trip that goes badly wrong, with bad weather and more chaos. The twist is that the rough trip actually brings them closer together. Greg realizes his dad just wanted to spend time with him, and the movie ends with the two of them sharing a genuine moment of connection as summer wraps up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and kid-friendly humor.
